notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed. The upstream environment and the sim path were not run: racecar_gym needs pybullet, numpy 1.22.3 and gymnasium 0.28.1 (requirements.txt) and downloads track scenes on first use, and package code never imports the clone. The fake backend is the package's own kinematic stand-in; it is not the pybullet vehicle and was not compared with it. It keeps the real observation keys, the 1080-ray lidar length and the two normalized actuator action bounds, but the dynamics, progress, reward, pose and lidar scan are placeholders. The contract states timestep 10 ms from the in-clone SimulationSpec default (racecar_gym/core/specs.py:8) and the fixed 0.01 s sensor scheduler (racecar_gym/bullet/providers.py:67); the downloaded scene supplies the world's actual time_step, so a deployment must re-check it. Determinism is statistical because sensor noise uses numpy's global generator, not the seeded np_random. env_id SingleAgentAustria-v0 is the documented predefined id; opening it with gymnasium.make would additionally need racecar_gym.envs.gym_api imported. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only sets the seed of the next reset, no native call) and five G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived integer/unitless inputs (ticks, the two seed inputs and the steering/motor arrays). G4 has no warnings. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. No hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
